_doc: ENCOUNTERS for The Squeeze. 'party' lists character ids from characters/ (empty = use the active campaign party). 'enemies' instantiate templates from enemies/enemies.json with per-instance overrides. bossPhases fire once when the referenced enemy drops below hpBelow. Balance targets baseline (no-resonance) damage: a fresh hero with ~300 HP and 3-4 starter abilities can win each fight on baseline damage alone.

encounters.name: The 4 AM Unload
encounters.description: Forty-eight feet of freight in a dead building. You versus the wall, with the ballast hum grinding in your ears.

encounters.name: Front-End Storm
encounters.description: The hour-occupancy dashboard is red, and management's pet is running the paging wand. Hold the floor.

encounters.name: The Manager's Office
encounters.description: The email is already out — a short 'not ready' note sitting in the area manager's inbox, sent before you ever walked in — and the man who sent it smiles behind the desk. Everything you built this act is on the line.

bossPhases.narrationText: The copy Mattie-T already sent — the one addressed to Cap'n Skagg — slithers across the desk like it was always there. It was.
The quarterly squeeze hits the store: hours slashed mid-shift, the crew scattered, and the board demanding blood. The building itself leans on you.

encounters.name: The Friday Oil Rush
encounters.description: Six bays, a line of pickups around the block, and the clock running on every one. The service shop's first big push — the honeymoon happens here, on your feet.

encounters.name: The Purge Audit
encounters.description: Jury's watch is on every bay and the retirement memo is already moving up the chain. The friendly air of the building condenses into something sharp.

encounters.name: The Brick Wall
encounters.description: The grievance grinds for a week and comes back with the only stamp the machine owns: yes, they said it, and no, it didn't happen.

bossPhases.narrationText: The denial is on the record in plain words, the way it was said to Adriana's face. Nothing is redacted. Nothing is admitted.
The investigator spoke to the very people who said it, accepted their denial at face value, and closed the file. The door was never a door.

encounters.name: The Christmas Party Slur
encounters.description: The rented community hall under fluorescent glare. Jury walks up with casual malice and says it twice, in front of witnesses. The second grievance is already signing itself.

bossPhases.narrationText: Twice, with witnesses, the word she used hangs in the party air. The second grievance is filed that same night.
Same stamp, same closed file, same lesson: truth, ethics, and human dignity do not exist inside this system. Only liability exists — so the apparatus will aggressively lie to protect itself.

encounters.name: The Body Keeps the Score
encounters.description: The burning nerve fire that flares across your forehead for the first time — shingles, the body's own scorecard for the year. Fight through it to pack the truck.

bossPhases.narrationText: The pain is a line of fire across your forehead, and it's honest where the store never was: it is telling you to leave.

encounters.name: The Neglected Bays
encounters.description: Six bays under a roof that hasn't been repainted since the previous decade, years of deferred maintenance, and a clock already running on your first ticket. The neglect is a living thing in the room with you.

encounters.name: The Executive Walkthrough
encounters.description: The executive pack descends on the building — six suits in polished shoes flanked by the Area Director. Stand before corporate scrutiny and hold the floor.

bossPhases.narrationText: Only the Store Manager walked with them. The rest of you guessed at the edicts from the floor, watching the glass doors close before a single question was asked.
Turn-time clocks, streamlined sign-offs, zero questions taken. The whole sold-out order lands on the bays at once.

encounters.name: Store Manager Azalia
encounters.description: Store Manager Azalia's weaponized kindness unmakes every consequence before the ink dries. Stand your ground against the smile that cancels accountability.

bossPhases.narrationText: Azalia smiles warmly as your write-up dissolves into pleasant apologies. Every consequence is unmade before the ink dries.
The conscientious workers carry everyone else's weight while Azalia protects the slackers with a reassuring pat on the shoulder.

encounters.name: The Scapegoat Investigation
encounters.description: A wheel came off in the lot and management needs a scapegoat. The District Safety Investigator sits across from you with a rewritten report, asking you to reconsider your signature.

bossPhases.narrationText: The report is rewritten, the witnesses reminded what they didn't see, the blame slid toward the manager who refused to sign.
The store needs a signature it can bury — and yours is the one it wants. The whole building leans on the pen.

encounters.name: The Regional Desk
encounters.description: Three hundred miles away behind phones and calendars, built to absorb complaints until they fossilize — but the complaint is already running past it, on a CC line that bypasses every smiling gatekeeper in the building.

bossPhases.narrationText: The complaint is already past the store, past the area desk, sitting on a regional calendar where the smile has no power.
For one small week the machine blinks when you push. Not justice. A crack. A crack is a start.

encounters.name: The Body Keeps the Score (Again)
encounters.description: The second outbreak — the same burning line across the same forehead, drawn where everyone can see it. One per state, one store per price paid. Fight through it to finish the load.

bossPhases.narrationText: The same line of fire across the forehead — the second entry on the body's ledger, written where everyone can see it.

encounters.name: The Front-End Swarm
encounters.description: Nine o'clock and six deep at every register, the service desk blinking, and no supervisor anywhere to page. Tell them their number, then save the five ahead of them.

encounters.name: The One-Man Close
encounters.description: Midnight: forty thousand square feet of dark, every till to count, every door to check — and the building, empty, pressing in like it's keeping count of you too.

bossPhases.narrationText: Every light you kill, every till you count — the dark grows one room deeper, one corner further, and no one is coming to help.
The supervisors' channel is dead air. It has been for eleven months. The close is yours alone, the way it always is.

encounters.name: The Blotter Regulars
encounters.description: Weekly visitors, a weather system: the team that sweeps housewares and electronics, and the grab-and-run that empties a shelf in eleven seconds.

encounters.name: The Claim Blizzard
encounters.description: Everyone claims on everyone: associate against associate, manager against associate, and a closing manager who files his own to stay out of the way.

encounters.name: The Parking Lot Draw
encounters.description: Eleven at night, a dispute walking to its cars, two hands going to two waistbands. The lot is dark, the line is thin, and it's yours to hold.

bossPhases.bannerText: THE HAND GOES TO THE WAIST
bossPhases.narrationText: Words fail first, then hands. The escalation is a live wire and the lot is dark — talk them down, walk them apart.
The line between this being your town's news and being nothing is thinner than you want to think about. Hold it.

encounters.name: The Freight-to-Floor
encounters.description: The overhaul hits the floor all at once — the dock, the bins, the topstock, the whole rebuild under a clock that wants it faster. Proves whether the system works when leadership equips its people.

bossPhases.narrationText: The trailers keep arriving. The wall keeps needing to fall. The floor keeps requiring feed. The machine wants it all at once.
The crew moves as one body — bin, dock, shelf, topstock — and the impossible number goes down. This is what leadership with protection looks like.

encounters.name: The Compliance Walkthrough
encounters.description: The operational walkthrough is under the microscope of the regional directors. With Richard and {hero} leading the floor together, stand tall against the audit pressure.

bossPhases.narrationText: A sharp technical question from the regional director. Richard and Todd step up in unison, breaking down the operational metrics with total precision.
The pressure mounts, but the freight floor holds firm. The execution speaks for itself.

encounters.name: Store Manager Jay-Dau
encounters.description: Friend by daylight, hell on the clock: Jay-Dau brings the quarterly corporate pressure to the floor, ready to sacrifice his best supervisor to save his own standing.

bossPhases.narrationText: The same man who laughs at your kitchen table hands you to the machine to save his standing. Two faces, one spine, both yours to survive.
The quarterly numbers need a sacrifice and the office needs a name. Jay-Dau decides who goes under the bus — unless the line holds.

encounters.name: Store Lead Amandy
encounters.description: The screaming assistant manager at full tilt: impossible demands, the re-done plan, and insults shouted within earshot of the crew. Hand the impossible number back done.

bossPhases.narrationText: Amandy screams a contradictory order over the radio, throwing the whole floor into panic. Stand your ground.

encounters.name: The Overnight Meat Grinder
encounters.description: Three in the morning: empty shelves, freight pallets breathing in the dark, and a whole building with no one to help. The grinder doesn't need to do anything. It just needs to be the only thing.

bossPhases.narrationText: One resigned, two walked out at 3 AM, three was let go, and the rest blurred into numbers — thirteen names you stopped learning because liking them cost too much.

bossPhases.bannerText: THE OVERNIGHT IS THE ONLY THING
bossPhases.narrationText: No supervisors. No backup. No end to the trailers. Just you, the dark, and the question the machine asks every manager it eats.

encounters.name: The Body Keeps the Score (Third Entry)
encounters.description: Outbreak Number Three: the same burning line across the same forehead, harder and hungrier. The body has been shouting for three years. Now it's screaming.

bossPhases.narrationText: Three stores, three states, three entries on the ledger the body keeps. The body has been telling you to leave since Lamar.

encounters.name: The Relocation Contract
encounters.description: The clawback, the repayment, the years of the machine leaning on you all at once — the collar that's been waiting since Lamar, asking you to put it on willingly.

bossPhases.narrationText: A lawyer's friendly tone on every page: Corporate pays for the move. Corporate also owns you — if you walk or they fire you, you owe it back, thousands of dollars.
Florida, in the sunshine, at the end of a two-hour drive in the dark — with a lease that talks like a leash. He knows what it is. He walks in anyway.

encounters.name: The Asphalt Gauntlet
encounters.description: I-95 south in the dead of night: brake-light walls, construction barriers, and the open road that takes an hour on a good night and three on a bad one. The geography of the act, armed.

bossPhases.narrationText: An accident a hundred miles ahead: the traffic congeals into a red wall, and the one-hour drive becomes three. The commute is a psychological torture test in its own right.
Driving north into the Florida sunrise after fourteen hours on the floor — the glare that blanks the road and the shoulders, the last mile home that takes forever.

encounters.name: The Green Meters
encounters.description: Three months of gold: the unload runs, the bins breathe, the board stays green. The machine finally working the way you always told them it could — a victory-light fight, the honeymoon in meter form.

encounters.name: Sriniviii's Morning Verdict
encounters.description: Every morning after a grueling overnight shift: standing before Store Manager Sriniviii. The honeymoon is over, the warmth is gone, and the goalposts are mounted firmly on wheels.

bossPhases.narrationText: You clear the freight; Sriniviii raises the target. You clean the floor; the target shifts. No finished store has ever satisfied a rolling metric.
The verdict, delivered to a man who just finished a perfect night: the ritual phrase designed to break your spirit one morning at a time.

encounters.name: Ohmar's Formal Office
encounters.description: The formal chair, the closed door, the biggest man in the building asking questions in a voice that never rises. The terror of the region, made flesh — a man who runs on the aggressive management style the area favors.

bossPhases.narrationText: He doesn't need to shout. He asks a question, waits, and the silence does the work. The walkie on his hip is a warning the whole building reads.
The phrase again, delivered flat. The interview is over; the verdict is not. He stands, and the door is next to your back.

encounters.name: The Ownerless Building
encounters.description: The store after everyone else has gone: three hours on a task nobody will ever check, then a fourth on the one beneath it. The building holds you not because it needs you, but because it can.

enemies.name: The Hum of the Empty Store

bossPhases.narrationText: Unofficial, unspoken, unbreakable: every day the shift 'runs long.' The clock becomes a hostage negotiator.
No boss, no checklist, no end. Just the fluorescent hum and the exit door — and the thought, once, that the drive home is only the halfway point of the machine.

encounters.name: The Fourth Signal
encounters.description: The body's scorecard, fourth entry: shingles erupting across the forehead in full agonizing force, the immune system at its absolute limit after the commute, the hostage hours, and the terror. Mandatory third-party medical leave.

bossPhases.narrationText: One, two, three — and now four. The body has run out of ways to say it other than this: across the brow, unignorable, on the face the interviewers will see.
The leave is not a mercy; it is a containment. The building wants you out of sight while it decides if you still fit the schedule.

encounters.name: The Redemption Schedule
encounters.description: The relocation contract in its rawest form: corporate's weapon to keep you driving south into the dark. Break the trap by reading between the lines — stepping down within the company instead of walking away.

bossPhases.narrationText: Walk away, get fired — either way, thousands back. The contract is a leash with a repayment schedule stamped on the collar.
Salt Lake is a plane ride plus a life away. The debt is a wall in every direction — except the one you build yourself.

encounters.name: The 3 AM
encounters.description: The darkest hour of the memoir: the alternative, fully formed, visiting night after night — the place, the time, the plan, the silence — offered like a solution to the morning. You do not defeat it with a spell. You refuse it with a name: Adriana.

enemies.name: The Hum of the Silent Store

bossPhases.narrationText: Two and a half weeks, every night, considered seriously and completely planned — an alternative to the morning. It appears with the hum, fully formed, patient.

The fog lifts on the face of the woman who needs him — and the alternative loses its patience, its arithmetic, its whole grip. The reason he refused it every single night, and the reason he refuses it now, for good.

encounters.endLine: You made it through the night.

encounters.name: The Parting Shot
encounters.description: The step-down is accepted without resistance — colder than screaming. And as the final act of malice, the whisper carries down the hall to the team lead: 'He'll be out of the company in two months anyway.' The last boss of the crucible.

bossPhases.narrationText: Management lets him go soft and quiet, the way a trap lets a spring go. The whisper is the only honest sentence they'll say all year — and it's about the exit, not the career.
They're wrong — and it doesn't matter if they're right. The machine doesn't get to write the epilogue. He's already walking out the north door.

encounters.name: The Pay Cut
encounters.description: Twenty-four thousand dollars a year, vanished in a single signed form. The depression isn't about the money — it's about watching the machine prove, once again, that there is no landing pad between the crushing altitude of salaried management and the floor.

bossPhases.narrationText: The form is signed. The salaried title is gone. Twenty-four thousand dollars a year, just like that — and the machine never even looked up from its own paperwork.
Back at the bottom of the hourly ladder, watching management treat workers as disposable — and knowing, quietly, that you were right all along. The vindication is real. So is the grief.

encounters.name: Store Manager Abdoolie
encounters.description: Abdoolie doesn't need to be Ohmar to be intimidating. The cadence is the same — flat declarative sentences, the pause before the question, the cold stillness of the room. Stand your ground and speak the truth.

bossPhases.narrationText: Abdoolie hasn't raised his voice once. He doesn't need to. That cadence — flat, certain, waiting — is a frequency the nervous system already knows by name.
This is not St. Augustine. Abdoolie is not Ohmar. Naming the difference is the only weapon left — and it works.

encounters.name: The Customer Gauntlet
encounters.description: Ten hours behind the service desk: complaints, demands, abusive returns, and the fluorescent grind of the front lines.

bossPhases.narrationText: A customer yells about a return. The line behind them snakes into the main aisle, relentless and indifferent.

encounters.name: The All-Hands Inquisition
encounters.description: An all-hands personnel meeting in an 8x10 office backed by a feed-through battery rack. Aussie's spreadsheet is angry, and he only has one tool: the collective threat.

bossPhases.narrationText: Aussie reads down the printout name by name, airing completion times while customers in Aisle 6 listen through the car batteries.
Individual times are declared a fraud; collective punishment is announced. If the team average slips, everyone's evaluation burns.

encounters.name: The Final Balance Sheet
encounters.description: Four shingles outbreaks. A $24,000 pay cut. Five states in eight years. The machine's ledger versus the one thing it could never enter: integrity intact, empathy intact, a life still in your hands.

bossPhases.narrationText: Four states. Four shingles. A salary. A marriage that survived anyway. The machine itemizes the damage and calls it a performance review.
The balance is not in the machine's favor. It cannot enter: the people protected, the associates who got home in one piece, the nights held together by one name. Adriana. This column wins.
